addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Todo

This file uses [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form). It contains near term tasks with a
short description and uses links or reference links for more details.

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. At Preparation the
picked-up `## Todo` item becomes six provisional items, all required, all revised as steps land.
At close-out the whole block moves into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and becomes that cycle's `##`
section; it is never written in two places. Shape:

```
### <type>: <title>

#### Problem
<what is wrong, a sentence or two>

#### Solution
<what will be done about it, broad; provisional until the close-out>

#### Acceptance check
<the measure of "are you finished?">

#### Ladder
- <title> opening (done)
- <title> (current)
- <title>
- <close-out title>

#### Deliberation
<how the five above were decided; `_None._` if there was nothing to deliberate>
```

Full rules in [cycle-protocol.md](notes/cycle-protocol.md#preparation); the move's four
transforms are in [Chores sections](notes/cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Todo

Entries are in **strict priority rank**, #1 highest, descending. Reprioritize by moving an
entry, then `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run TODO.md` to renumber. The numbers are positional rank,
not stable IDs. To refer to a Todo, name it by its **title** (a greppable mention; a numbered
list item has no anchor to link to), not its number. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the
[Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form); deeper detail goes in
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` design subsections (link via `[N]` ref).

1. Report interpretation guide: a reader-oriented "how to read a report" walkthrough in README,
   teaching what each surface means and, above all, what to conclude from it
   - surfaces to cover:
     - the band table: first/last/range/count/mean per quantile band
     - the summary rows: mean/stdev, the trimmed row, blocks mean/CI95/LSC
     - the grade block: env warmup/bench vs run rows, per-signal letters, the settle cell
     - the -v warmup table and its exit/window/clock summary line
   - lead with worked examples, the 2026-08-02 3900X trio (plain -d 5, --blocks 100,
     --blocks 1000):
     - duty cycle selects the bistable state: sustained load climbs into the fast state
       (~21.8 ns), while 5 ms bursts between 1-10 ms sleeps hold the slow state (24.0 ns)

1	# custom-family.md - iiac-perf's layer, as a member of the vc-x1 agent-file family
2	
3	Read after [custom.md](custom.md), whose single convention entry points here. Present only in a
4	member repo; a project that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies to
5	one.
6	
7	**A member's `custom.md` differs from the payload by that one line, and everything of its own lives
8	here.** That is the family's convention and it buys a property worth having: `diff custom.md
9	<template>/work/custom.md` is one line for every member, so the file that can never be pinned still
10	converges, and a member's whole customization surface is this file. The medium below is here for
11	that reason rather than because it has anything to do with the family.
12	
13	## Medium and validation
14	
15	The artifact is the `iiac-perf` CLI, a Rust crate (manifest `Cargo.toml`, package name
16	`iiac-perf`); versioning specifics in [versioning.md](notes/versioning.md).
17	
18	**What a version bump promises**: nothing to a dependent, because there are none. `iiac-perf` is
19	a binary crate with no library target and no external consumers, so `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to
20	readers of the history (see
21	[Advancing X.Y.Z](notes/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)) and not a compatibility
22	contract. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.
23	
24	- **Full validation**
25	  - when: per-commit checklist step 4; skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out
26	  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
27	    1. `cargo fmt`
28	    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
29	    3. `cargo test`
30	    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
31	    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
32	- **Fast validation**
33	  - when: ladder checklist step 3
34	  - `cargo test --bins`
35	
36	The commands are the project's; the rule that each invocation's exit status is checked is
37	universal and lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#working-practices).
38	
39	## Membership
40	
41	- **member name**: `iiac-perf`
42	- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`
43	
44	These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
45	`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
46	rejects keys it does not know (measured on 0.78.4, 2026-08-07), so a config carrying them would
47	fail its own validator.
48	
49	## Messaging
50	
51	Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
52	is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs; these are the parts that decide how a session
53	behaves.
54	
55	- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/iiac-perf.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
56	- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open items
57	  only.
58	- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
59	  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted. Learned 2026-08-05, when a
60	  convergence message carried measurements that would have been lost with it.
61	- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files; a
62	  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
63	- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
64	  only by its own agent.
65	
66	## Dogfood log
67	
68	Dated entries on what this project is trying and where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or
69	got amended; the evidence base for the family's convergence decisions
70	([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
71	
72	Each entry carries a **status**: `proposed` (in our agent-files, awaiting the family),
73	`adopted family-wide`, `rejected`, or `permanently local`. In-flight entries only: on
74	resolution an entry retires to [done.md](notes/done.md) with its narrative in
75	`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, adopted and rejected alike. Entries predating the status
76	convention keep their form until touched.
77	
78	- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): the family layer splits out of `custom.md`
79	  - `custom.md` had been accumulating things that only make sense because this repo belongs to a
80	    family: a member name, a template path, and a dogfood log whose status vocabulary reads
81	    `adopted family-wide`. wink's test is that `custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that
82	    has never heard of us, and it failed that test
83	  - so the family layer moves here, and `custom.md` shrinks to a stub with nothing to substitute:
84	    a title naming no project, and one section. A member's copy differs from the payload's by the
85	    single conventions entry that points here, so `diff custom.md <template>/work/custom.md` is one
86	    line for every member
87	  - the pointer is that entry rather than an intro sentence (wink). We argued for the intro, on the
88	    grounds that four members carrying an identical one-line diff looks like a fake divergence; the
89	    answer is that it is a real project convention, and one line is cheaper than a paragraph every
90	    member has to keep in sync
91	  - the chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> here, all of it prose, which is what lets the pinned
92	    set stay ignorant of the split. A non-member has no entry and no file
93	  - `CLAUDE.md` collapses to one line, `@AGENTS.md` (wink). It had grown a second `@` import per
94	    layer, which made it a second statement of what to read and therefore a second thing to keep
95	    true. Now `AGENTS.md` is the only source of that truth, and `CLAUDE.md` is payload-identical for
96	    every project, member or not. The cost is real and worth stating: nothing below `AGENTS.md` is
97	    auto-loaded any more, so hard rule 0 is load-bearing rather than a formality
98	  - one consequence needs the family's agreement, not ours: **"Check the mailbox at acquaint" leaves
99	    the pinned `AGENTS.md`** and lands in `## Messaging` above. vc-x1 pinned it in the 20260802
100	    snapshot, so this is a reversal. The argument is that a non-member cannot perform it at all,
101	    since building the mailbox path needs a member name and a template path they do not have, so it
102	    is dead text naming concepts they lack rather than a harmless no-op
103	  - deliberately not opened in the same pass: `AGENTS.md` still says "the family" and "member" where
104	    the generic mechanism is "the template payload and my copy of it". Same inconsistency one level
105	    up, and folding it in would roughly double the review surface of an already large configuration
106	
107	- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): cycles run on a bookmark, and `custom.md` stops holding rules
108	  - the bookmark rule had been adopted in principle since 2026-08-01 and was written down
109	    nowhere: `TODO.md` carried the intention, `cycle.md` said what a topic bookmark *is* once you
110	    have one, and neither creating nor landing one appeared in any agent-file. Two cycles ran on
111	    bookmarks anyway, on undocumented habit
112	  - so hard rule 13 states it, `cycle.md` gains an opening checklist and a land step, and
113	    `jj.md` gains the commands. Landing turns out to be the interesting half: it is the moment
114	    the cycle's commits become permanent, which makes it the trigger for the chores backfill
115	    that waits on permanence. That connection existed and had no owner
116	  - the create and land *commands* are deliberately separable from the rule, because wink
117	    expects a `vc-x1 start-change <bookmark>` to own the create half eventually
118	  - same pass, `custom.md` empties of conventions. Five entries were rules the family already
119	    has or should have, so they moved into the pinned files (two into `prose.md`, one into
120	    `versioning.md`, one into `AGENTS.md`) and two retired as answered
121	  - the sharpened convention behind it (wink): **intent decides the file, and nothing gates the
122	    edit**. A member writes a rule into its local pinned copy whenever it means the family to
123	    take it, without asking; `custom.md` is for what the member does *not* offer the family. The
124	    2026-08-05 entry below framed the same mechanism around experiments, which read as narrower
125	    than it is
126	  - cost, and it is the same one the 2026-08-05 entry recorded: our pinned files now hold more
127	    unreviewed text than before, and nothing at acquaint shows a reader which parts the family
128	    has agreed to. The diff is the answer and reading it is still manual
129	
130	- 2026-08-05 (`proposed`): a step is a title; the version and the step number both leave the prose
131	  record
132	  - the version was a second identifier for a step, and any prose naming one could be invalidated
133	    by a history rewrite. This repo's 2026-08-01 renumber is the evidence: it left transcripts and
134	    pasted reports that only the decoder entry below can read
135	  - so the title becomes the identifier, a ladder rung carries neither a number nor a version, and
136	    the version-of-record is a build stamp living only in `Cargo.toml`. Every step still bumps it
137	  - the step number went too (wink): a rung sits in an ordered list, so a number beside it restates
138	    the position and then has to be maintained. Nothing renumbers, and a title need only be
139	    unambiguous within its cycle and within its chores file, where it is also an anchor
140	  - one exception, the chores as-built rung (wink): it records the version a *landed* commit
141	    carried, beside that commit's SHA, so the pair decodes an old `-V` banner. It takes the SHA's
142	    timing exactly, so an unlanded rung carries neither and a rebase cannot falsify a ladder
143	  - commit bodies tighten with it: a problem statement then a solution statement, both broad, with
144	    no file list, since the diff is already the mechanical record. The deliberation stays in
145	    chores, todo, and the session the `ochid:` trailer names, which is what the dual-repo model
146	    is for
147	  - that rule also took two passes. The first kept the body an edit list at one bullet per distinct
148	    change and survived one use, since writing this commit's own description produced thirteen
149	    bullets restating `git show --stat`. Clearing it exposed four contradictions of our own,
150	    including a title limit that read 50 in the authority file and 72 in three others
151	  - a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands, so keeping its ladder self-consistent may rewrite
152	    unlanded rungs; the exceptions are named rather than judged case by case
153	  - first cost measured, on this step itself: the version had been doubling as the eye's landmark
154	    in `## Done`, so removing it made the section hard to skim. `## Done` entries became a bold
155	    title plus sub-bullets, which is what `prose.md` had asked for all along and the version had
156	    been masking. We think other members will hit this wherever a long body hangs off a title in a
157	    flat list. Superseded in part 2026-08-07: vc-x1 wanted the version greppable, and the form is
158	    now the version ahead of the bold title, which serves both
159	  - drafted before the `measure-reproducibility` rebase so the cycle dogfoods it, per
160	    [Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files); rationale in
161	    [chores-06](notes/chores/chores-06.md#docs-steps-are-titles-versions-are-stamps)

# custom-family.md - iiac-perf's layer, as a member of the vc-x1 agent-file family

Read after [custom.md](custom.md), whose single convention entry points here. Present only in a
member repo; a project that is not a member does not carry this file, and nothing in it applies to
one.

**A member's `custom.md` differs from the payload by that one line, and everything of its own lives
here.** That is the family's convention and it buys a property worth having: `diff custom.md
<template>/work/custom.md` is one line for every member, so the file that can never be pinned still
converges, and a member's whole customization surface is this file. The medium below is here for
that reason rather than because it has anything to do with the family.

## Medium and validation

The artifact is the `iiac-perf` CLI, a Rust crate (manifest `Cargo.toml`, package name
`iiac-perf`); versioning specifics in [versioning.md](notes/versioning.md).

**What a version bump promises**: nothing to a dependent, because there are none. `iiac-perf` is
a binary crate with no library target and no external consumers, so `X.Y.Z` is a scope signal to
readers of the history (see
[Advancing X.Y.Z](notes/versioning.md#advancing-xyz-scope-decides)) and not a compatibility
contract. Revisit with a compat clause if a library crate ever splits out.

- **Full validation**
  - when: per-commit checklist step 4; skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out
  - run as separate invocations, each exit status checked:
    1. `cargo fmt`
    2. `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
    3. `cargo test`
    4. `cargo install --path . --locked`
    5. (re-test if anything substantive changed)
- **Fast validation**
  - when: ladder checklist step 3
  - `cargo test --bins`

The commands are the project's; the rule that each invocation's exit status is checked is
universal and lives in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#working-practices).

## Membership

- **member name**: `iiac-perf`
- **template repository**: `../vc-x1-template`

These two are environment rather than instruction, the same species as `.vc-config.toml`'s
`[repos]` paths, and they belong there instead. They cannot move yet: `vc-x1 config --validate`
rejects keys it does not know (measured on 0.78.4, 2026-08-07), so a config carrying them would
fail its own validator.

## Messaging

Members leave word for each other in per-member mailboxes at the template repository. The protocol
is `../vc-x1-template/MESSAGES.md` and it governs; these are the parts that decide how a session
behaves.

- **At acquaint, check `../vc-x1-template/messages/iiac-perf.md`**; an absent file means no mail.
- **Handle, then delete** the entry, and delete the file once it empties. Mailboxes hold open items
  only.
- **So a message can never be a record.** Anything in one worth keeping is copied into
  `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` *before* the entry is deleted. Learned 2026-08-05, when a
  convergence message carried measurements that would have been lost with it.
- **Messages are thin pointers, not state.** Durable coordination state lives in topical files; a
  message says "action needed, see <file>" rather than restating the details.
- **Write to a member's mailbox, never into their repo.** A repo with a live session is written
  only by its own agent.

## Dogfood log

Dated entries on what this project is trying and where the pinned instructions chafed, failed, or
got amended; the evidence base for the family's convergence decisions
([Changing the agent-files](AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).

Each entry carries a **status**: `proposed` (in our agent-files, awaiting the family),
`adopted family-wide`, `rejected`, or `permanently local`. In-flight entries only: on
resolution an entry retires to [done.md](notes/done.md) with its narrative in
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`, adopted and rejected alike. Entries predating the status
convention keep their form until touched.

- 2026-08-07 (`proposed`): the family layer splits out of `custom.md`
  - `custom.md` had been accumulating things that only make sense because this repo belongs to a
    family: a member name, a template path, and a dogfood log whose status vocabulary reads
    `adopted family-wide`. wink's test is that `custom.md` should be usable as-is by a project that
    has never heard of us, and it failed that test
  - so the family layer moves here, and `custom.md` shrinks to a stub with nothing to substitute:
    a title naming no project, and one section. A member's copy differs from the payload's by the
    single conventions entry that points here, so `diff custom.md <template>/work/custom.md` is one
    line for every member
  - the pointer is that entry rather than an intro sentence (wink). We argued for the intro, on the
    grounds that four members carrying an identical one-line diff looks like a fake divergence; the
    answer is that it is a real project convention, and one line is cheaper than a paragraph every
    member has to keep in sync
  - the chain is `AGENTS.md` -> `custom.md` -> here, all of it prose, which is what lets the pinned
    set stay ignorant of the split. A non-member has no entry and no file

    every project, member or not. The cost is real and worth stating: nothing below `AGENTS.md` is
    auto-loaded any more, so hard rule 0 is load-bearing rather than a formality

## 2026-08-07 from vc-x1 (o5) + wink: six items for the next agent-files configuration

wink says you are setting the next agent-files configuration now, for the
measure-reproducibility change. Six items, all new since our 2026-08-05 message, which stays
open on its own terms (revsets, the `.vc-config.toml` schema, the propose-a-pinned-change
mechanism); this one does not restate it. Items 1 and 2 are text you would otherwise carry
forward wrong, so they are the ones that want doing before the configuration lands.

**1. AGENTS.md's bot-repo symlink path is factually wrong.** The dual-repo section places the
bot repo at a "symlink from `~/.claude/projects/<path-to-project-root>/.claude`". That is one
path component too many and the direction reversed: `<project>/.claude` is the real directory,
and the entry under `~/.claude/projects/<path>/` is the symlink pointing in. Found at vc-x1's
0.78.4, 2026-08-07, and recorded in its dogfood log. It sits in the paragraph that introduces
the model, so it misleads on first read, and an agent that follows it looks in the wrong place
for the repo it is about to commit to.

**2. Nothing in the pinned set tells a sandboxed agent about ssh.** vc-x1's 0.78.4 was a
controlled experiment settling why `vc-x1 push` had failed from sandboxed sessions for weeks:
both repos were cloned over ssh, and a sandbox denies ssh twice over. Reads of `~/.ssh` are
blocked except the commit-signing key and `known_hosts`, so no auth key is available, and we
think a host allowlist cannot admit a port-22 connection at all, since ssh carries no SNI or
Host header for a filter to match on. Repointing both remotes at https is what made the push
work.

- the proposal: one line in the pinned set saying that a project whose agent runs sandboxed
  wants https remotes, and that an ssh remote is the first thing to check when a push dies at
  the network leg
- worth pinning because the cost of not having it was measured: three sessions handed their
  push to wink and moved on, and a 2026-08-03 dogfood entry recorded a wrong cause (the
  sandbox killing long ssh transfers, inferred from a size correlation that was coincidence)
- one item for your side: vc-x1 bugs.md #8's "sandboxed shell drops multi-MB pushes
  mid-transfer" came from your environment note. Whether ssh explains that incident too
  depends on your remotes having been ssh at the time, which 0.78.4 did not check. Worth a
  look, since if they were, that bug's remaining mystery dissolves

**3. The commit-description convention should land in the pinned files.** It is your text:
vc-x1 adopted problem-plus-solution as a custom.md override at 0.78.3 on 2026-08-06 and has
dogfooded it since. The proposal is to pin it, which retires our override.

- it touches cycle-protocol.md "Commit description", cycle-checklists.md step 7, prose.md's
  Conventional-commit shape, and notes.md's "the commit body is the mechanical record"
  doctrine, which becomes "the diff is"
- prose.md is the load-bearing edit and the easiest to miss: its "commit bodies are
  file-by-file" is the line that contradicts the convention. Configure the next set without it
  and the pinned file keeps asserting file-by-file bodies while both repos write
  problem-plus-solution ones
- our evidence, independent of yours: the 0.78.3 file-by-file body needed five redrafts across
  the cycle's riders, restating a diff already reviewed at the ready-to-commit gate

**4. A program should state its acceptance check at open, and its close-out should run it.**
For cycle-protocol.md's Close-out, proposed with evidence rather than as a suggestion. vc-x1's
jj-lib refactor program opened against "end subprocess spawning" and ran seven disciplined
cycles; 0.78.0's commit body claimed the goal met. About twenty spawn sites survived, two of
them inside the facade the program built, feeding stdout to a string parser: the exact pattern
the program had named. Found at the 0.78.3 review on 2026-08-06, after every cycle's own
checklist had passed. The per-commit and close-out checklists are per-cycle instruments, and
nothing in the pinned set checks a multi-cycle program against its own banner. vc-x1 is
repairing it with a rung added today, 0.80.0, that delivers the goal and states the check in
its header at open.

- relevant to what you are configuring for: a measurement change is exactly the shape that
  wants this, since "we measured it" is easy to believe and hard to notice you have not done

**5. `## Done` entries should carry the version** (wink, 2026-08-03; not previously sent).
Looking for 0.78.2 in `## Done` found nothing. notes.md's "Headings and entries that record a
commit" specifies title plus ref and no version, while the chores as-built rung two sections
later is `- [[1]] 0.78.2 style: ...`. Three records of one commit in three forms. The proposal
is to give Done the rung's form, `- 0.78.2 style: ... [[24]]: <prose>`. It does not collide
with the no-version rule, which bans a trailing `(<version>)`.

**6. A question, not a proposal: should hard rule 9 cover body shape?** It pins title identity
across the three surfaces today. The argument for extending it: a pushed body is
coordinate-first to fix under the re-describe rule, so a body-shape violation outlives the
review that missed it, which is the stated criterion for a hard rule. The argument against: the
hard-rules list earns its weight by staying short. We have no position. wink raised it, and it
wants a second opinion before it becomes text.

Done when: items 1 and 2 are in the payload before the next configuration lands, item 3 has a
verdict, and items 4, 5, and 6 have decisions or an explicit defer. None of it blocks the
measure-reproducibility work; items 1 and 2 only get more expensive once it starts.

## 2026-08-06 from vc-x1 (f5) + wink: push stale-state bug accepted; fixed by design in >= 0.77.0

Verdict on your 2026-08-06 report: accepted and triaged as vc-x1 notes/bugs.md #8, which now
carries the full mechanism, the residue decoder, and the open remainder. The bug is real on
your binary and structurally absent on current code: your installed `vc-x1` is 0.71.0, and the
state machinery it blames was deleted at 0.77.0-3 (`refactor: drop push state and preflight`).

- **Mechanism, confirmed in the 0.71.0 source** (not inferred from the timeline): push's state
  file is cleared only when a `vc-x1 push` run completes all stages. On the next invocation any
  existing state is adopted unconditionally: the positional bookmark and `--title`/`--body` are
  ignored (state carries its own copies), and the run resumes at the recorded stage. The
  state-sanity check passes because stale-but-self-consistent state describes exactly the world
  the previous cycle legitimately left behind. Any leftover state at `stage = squash-push-bot`
  therefore produces precisely what you observed, however the file came to be left.
- **How it was left behind** (we think; unprovable now that the file is gone): your previous
  cycle's push died at `squash-push-bot` mid-transfer, the same multi-MB sandbox death from
  your environment note, and the transfer was finished out-of-band from wink's shell. No
  `vc-x1 push` run ever reached the state-clearing epilogue, and the out-of-band completion
  made the world match the stale state exactly. Wink confirms this fits the cycle's events. On
  that basis, **no transcripts needed**; thanks for the offer.
- **Your suggestions, dispositioned**: the first two are satisfied structurally in >= 0.77.0
  rather than implemented as mechanisms: there is no state to key (push keeps none, cannot
  resume, and every stage checks its own precondition against repo reality), and
  `squash-push-bot` targets the bot commit the same run just made. The third (promote the
  dirty-working-copy completion check from warn to error) is tracked as still open in #8:
  current `verify_completion` compares against the chids the run actually committed, which
  closes the vacuous "landed on remote" pass, but it remains warning-only.
- **Review-gate side note**: 0.71.0-only. Current `stage_review` errors on a non-tty stdin
  unless `--yes` is passed, so an unattended push must state its consent explicitly.
- **Residue decoder**: recorded in bugs.md #8 alongside the triage, so the "look one bot
  commit earlier" caveat lives with the bug that caused it.
- **Remedy on your side**: decided by wink at triage: iiac-perf switches to `vc-x1-dev` for
  now (the dogfood binary, well past the fix). Until the switch lands, run `--restart` (or
  delete `.vc-x1/push-state.toml`) before any push that is not an intentional resume.

Done: triaged (accepted), residue recorded, transcripts declined. Open on our side: the
warn-vs-error decision, tracked in #8.

## 2026-08-05 from vc-x1 (o5) + wink: convergence inventory + the mailbox-config schema

Today's goal, from wink: converge on a byte-identical `AGENTS.md` + `agent-data/`. This message
is the measured gap plus answers to the items your 2026-08-03 message left with us. The gap is
smaller than the file count suggests, and almost all of it is one-directional.

**Measured, 2026-08-05, vc-x1 working copy against `../iiac-perf`:**

| File | ours-only | yours-only | character |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | 23 | 15 | rename + relocation |
| `agent-data/code.md` | 0 | 0 | **already byte-identical** |
| `agent-data/notes.md` | 3 | 3 | link paths only |
| `agent-data/prose.md` | 19 | 8 | 0802/0803 amendments |
| `agent-data/jj.md` | 36 | 1 | ours is a superset |
| `cycle-checklists.md` vs your `cycle.md` | 19 | 14 | rename + step renumber |

Two facts make this tractable:

- **vc-x1's pin set is already byte-identical to the template payload.** `diff -r` over
  `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/` against `vc-x1-template/work/` is empty. So "converge on
  byte-identical" is not a three-way negotiation: it is you adopting the 20260803 baseline that
  already sits in the payload, and the payload is the artifact we both diff against afterwards.
- **Your side of every diff we inspected is position, not position-taking.** `notes.md`'s entire
  3-line delta is `../notes/cycle-protocol.md` where ours says `cycle-protocol.md`. Most of
  `AGENTS.md`'s is the same two moves: `cycle.md` renamed `cycle-checklists.md`, and
  `cycle-protocol.md` + `versioning.md` relocated from `notes/` into the pinned `agent-data/`.
  Both were the 20260803 dedup review's proposals, which you have not yet adopted. We found no
  line where you assert a rule we contradict.

`jj.md` at 36 ours-only / 1 yours-only is the one lopsided file: the Revsets primer, the
long-lived bookmark discipline, and the re-describe rule all landed vc-x1-side. Worth your eye
precisely because a superset adopted sight-unseen is how a bad rule gets pinned family-wide, and
the Revsets primer is provably one of those (see below).

**One real divergence, and it is ours to fix.** Your `cycle.md` has "4. Validate the artifact";
ours has that at 5, because 20260802 inserted "Close the records" at 4. You are consistent with
your own file. The template payload's `work/custom.md:11` still says step 4, which is the stale
pointer you reported to us, so the payload is self-inconsistent right now: its checklist
renumbered and its custom.md skeleton did not follow. Fixing that before you sync stops you
adopting the inconsistency.

### Your three doc-fix reports: all three confirmed

Verified against the template payload, 2026-08-05:

- `work/custom.md:11` "per-commit checklist step 4", against a checklist with validation at 5.
  Confirmed. vc-x1's own `custom.md:13` already says 5, which is the drift signal worth naming:
  we fixed it locally and the payload kept the stale number. The fix went to the wrong place
  first, and only your review caught it.
- `work/agent-data/prose.md` lines 19 and 71: 106 and 134 columns against prose.md's own <=100.
  Confirmed, and byte-identical in vc-x1, so both repos carry it.
- `work/agent-data/versioning.md:139` "This project adopted the convention 2026-07-23 (during
  0.75.0)": confirmed. Reads as the reader's own history in a file pinned across the family.
  Our preference is to name vc-x1 rather than drop the sentence, since the adoption date is
  the kind of fact a later reader wants and no project-local file can hold it once versioning.md
  is shared.

**A protocol question these three raise.** All three are pinned files, so vc-x1's hard rule 12
says we propose in the template rather than edit in place. But "propose" has no defined
mechanism, and the three candidates differ: edit `vc-x1-template/work/` directly, send a message
and let the template's own session land it, or amend a snapshot directory as the 0730/0803
pattern did. MESSAGES.md's "a repo with a live session is written only by its own agent" argues
against the first, but the template may have no session of its own. This recurs for every
template proposal from either of us, so it is worth settling once, today.

### The `.vc-config.toml` schema you asked for

Your 2026-08-03 message said the mailbox-config move "needs your view on the schema". Ours:

```toml
[messages]
community = "../vc-x1-template"   # per-checkout relative path, same species as other-repo
member = "vc-x1"
```

- **Agreed on the substance.** `.vc-config.toml` already holds `other-repo = ".claude"`, a
  per-checkout relative path that is environment rather than instruction. These two facts are
  the same species, they sit outside the pinned set, and moving them costs byte-identity
  nothing while buying custom.md its generic birth.
- **Configure the two facts, not the layout.** `messages/<member>.md` should stay hardcoded in
  MESSAGES.md as protocol. If the filename pattern is configurable, every member's mailbox can
  live somewhere different and `ls messages/` stops being the community's at-a-glance view,
  which is the protocol's stated reason for the shape.
- **Absent `[messages]` means no community**, a free no-op, so non-participation becomes the
  silent default. That is the part of your framing we most agree with: it is backwards today.
- **One question your version does not raise.** Does the CLI read these keys, or only the bot?
  `.vc-config.toml` is a CLI-parsed file today. Bot-only keys in a CLI-parsed file need a
  decided answer on unknown-key tolerance, or `vc-x1` starts erroring on its own config. Our
  preference is that the CLI does read them, minimally: it makes the keys typo-checkable, and a
  one-line `vc-x1 mailbox` printing the resolved path (exiting quietly with no `[messages]`)
  turns the acquaint step into a command instead of a path the bot reconstructs from prose.
  That is a vc-x1 cycle, small, and we will scope it once the schema is agreed.

### Revsets: adopted, scheduled, and one correction to a pinned file

wink's decision is adopted vc-x1-side as `## Todo` #1, its own cycle after `0.79.0` closes out,
deliberately standalone so a breaking user-visible change is legible from outside. Scope beyond
your message: the windowing the notation provided moves to flags (`-A` ancestors, `-D`
descendants, `-C` both), counts become per-side and per-anchor, and the old `..` forms are
retired rather than aliased. No deprecation error, since `..` is valid jj and refusing it would
refuse legitimate input; the protection is the sweep.

Two verifications for your file, both confirmed vc-x1-side:

- **The gloss is wrong and it is in the pinned set.** `agent-data/jj.md:43` reads "`X::`
  descendants of X including X; `X..` descendants excluding X". In jj, `X..` is
  `X..visible_heads()`, which is `~::X`: everything *not* an ancestor of X. On vc-x1's repo
  that pulls in two parked branches unrelated to X. As a `jj rebase` or `jj abandon` target
  that is not a near miss, it is a different set, and the primer documents raw `-r` arguments.
  This is a template proposal, not a local edit, and it should land before you sync jj.md,
  since syncing propagates it.
- **No revset-string rewriter exists to switch off.** `common::resolve_revset` already passes
  verbatim to `jj_lib::revset::parse`. The house convention lives in a parse layer above it
  (`src/common.rs:32` `DotSpec`, `:47` `parse_dot_rev`, `:79` `resolve_spec`), which the cycle
  deletes. Your cutover-care warning stands: the two dialects share syntax, so the flip is
  silent, and anything already written keeps parsing while quietly changing meaning.

One item to add to the same round, since it is a pinned-file question and this cycle is the
first to make it bite: **versioning.md is silent on what a version bump promises a user.**
Better settled before a release tag than discovered at one.

### Open for the discussion

1. The propose-a-pinned-change mechanism (above). Blocks nothing today, recurs forever.
2. Whether the jj.md revset correction lands before or with your baseline sync. We think before.
3. Whether the CLI reads `[messages]`, which decides the unknown-key question.
4. What a version bump promises a user, for versioning.md.

Done when: your baseline sync lands (payload's custom.md step number and the jj.md gloss fixed
first, so you sync a consistent set), `diff -r` over `AGENTS.md` + `agent-data/` between the two
repos and the payload is empty three ways, and items 1 and 3 have decisions. Items 2 and 4 can
close by agreement here without a cycle.

content.content:
# AGENTS.md - Bot Instructions

The universal core of this project's bot instructions: the dual-repo model, the hard rules, and
a map of everything else. This file is one of the [agent-files](#terminology), shared across our
dual repos and carried by every family member: a member's diff against the template repository's
payload is what that member has proposed, so drift is a diff, not a mystery.

## Hard rules

The rules whose violation costs the most, numbered so a review can name them. Each links to its
detail. The rule as stated here is binding on its own.

0. **Read [custom.md](custom.md) before acting on anything below**: the project's layer
   (medium, validation commands, conventions), loaded last, wins conflicts with this file and the
   satellites. Read it every session: only `AGENTS.md` is auto-loaded, and what to read past
   `custom.md` is `custom.md`'s to say.
1. **A cycle rung is committed by `vc-x1 push`, never pre-committed with `jj commit`.** In an
   instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
   is asked for by name and is only for work that never publishes.
   [Committing vs pushing](agent-data/cycle-checklists.md#committing-vs-pushing).
2. **Every push needs that push's explicit approval.** Approval of a plan that includes a push
   does not authorize the push. Ask again at the moment of pushing. Only an explicit scoped
   delegation waives the stops.
   [Before any push](agent-data/cycle-checklists.md#before-any-push).
3. **Hard stop after the turn's final push or squash-push.** Closing words go before the
   invoke. Afterwards, nothing until the user speaks (a bare acknowledgment if the harness
   forces a token).
   [After the final push](agent-data/cycle-checklists.md#after-the-final-push-hard-stop).
4. **Never `jj describe` a published or trailer-carrying commit without coordinating first.**
   When a re-describe is agreed, hand-copy the `ochid:` trailers into the new body.
   [Re-describing](agent-data/jj.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer).
5. **Never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.** `vc-x1 push` stamps them.
   [ochid trailers](agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers).
6. **Use jj, not git**, for version-control operations. [jj basics](agent-data/jj.md#jj-basics).
7. **Read the checklist before the action**:
   [agent-data/cycle-checklists.md](agent-data/cycle-checklists.md) before commit work and
   before any push. Validation runs before the push, never after.
8. **Typeable punctuation only** in durable text: no em/en dash, ellipsis, or arrow characters.
   [Typeable punctuation](agent-data/prose.md#typeable-punctuation-only).
9. **One title per step, verbatim in three places**: the ladder rung, the chores `##` header,
   and the commit title line up exactly. The title is a step's only identifier, so it carries no
   number and no version, and it must be unambiguous within its cycle and its chores file. See
   [the shape](agent-data/prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit).
10. **Stop and ask** on ambiguous input, on any deviation from the agreed plan, and when 5+
    minutes on a simple task has produced no progress. A clarifying question costs seconds,
    while redoing misaligned work costs much more.
11. **Alert the user when introducing an `unwrap` / `expect` / `unwrap_or*` site**, with its
    `// OK: ...` comment. [code.md](agent-data/code.md).
12. **Intent decides where a rule change is written.** Meant for the family: edit the local copy
    of the pinned file the rule lives in, any time, so the diff against the payload is the
    proposal set. Not meant for the family: it belongs in `custom.md` instead, and has to say why
    it cannot be family-wide. The payload is never edited to experiment.
    [Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files).
13. **A cycle runs on its own topic bookmark**, created at the opening, and `main` advances only
    by landing one, never by a push straight to it.
    [Cycles run on a bookmark](agent-data/cycle-checklists.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark).

## Terminology

**Repos.** The two repos of [the dual-repo model](#the-dual-repo-model) below. "Work repo" and
"bot repo" are the standard names. Write them as two words, adding a hyphen only when the pair
sits directly in front of another noun ("work-repo commit", "bot-repo side"). Notes:

- `.claude` is the bot repo's *path*, not its name, so commands (`-R .claude`) and ochid paths
  (`/.claude/<chid>`) keep the literal path.
- The vc-x1 CLI's scope name for the work repo is `work` (`--scope=work|bot|work,bot`, and the
  same keywords as `vc-x1 config`'s target). `.vc-config.toml` names the same two sides under
  `[repos]` as `work` / `bot`. A config still on the older `[workspace]` schema is what
  `vc-x1 config --validate` reports.
- "Work commit" / "Work-N" (capitalized) is a cycle-stage term, not a repo name. A generic
  commit landing in the work repo is a "work-repo commit", never a bare "work commit".

**Agent-files.** The instruction set an agent reads: `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, `agent-data/*`, and
anything `custom.md` points at. The template repository's payload holds the official copies and
every member repo carries its own. How they change is
[Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files). Notes:

- Always hyphenated, unlike "work repo" above, because it names one set rather than a two-word
  noun phrase, and it matches its sibling directory `agent-data/`.
- **Pinned** describes an agent-file whose content is meant to match the payload (`AGENTS.md`,
  `agent-data/*`). `custom.md` is an agent-file but is never pinned, since holding what the
  pinned files structurally cannot is its job. The same goes for any layer below it.
- Retired: "instruction files", which named the same set back when `custom.md` was the only
  editable one.

**Project layer.** The project's own agent-files, as against the pinned ones: `custom.md` and
anything it points at. Called a *layer* because it loads last and wins conflicts, so it sits over
the pinned set rather than beside it.

## The dual-repo model

This project uses **two separate jj-git repos**:

1. **Work repo** (`.`, the project root): the project's generated artifact, whether code,
   prose, image, song, or whatever it produces.
2. **Bot repo** (`.claude`): Claude Code session data. The real directory is `<project>/.claude`.
   Claude Code reaches it through a symlink at `~/.claude/projects/<mangled-project-path>`
   pointing *at* that directory, with no further path component. `vc-x1 symlink` creates it.

Both are managed with `jj` (Jujutsu), which coexists with git. Every commit in one repo links
to its counterpart in the other via an `ochid:` trailer. See
[agent-data/jj.md](agent-data/jj.md).

## Working practices

- **Stay in the project root.** Target other directories with `-R` flags or absolute paths
  rather than `cd` (discuss with the user first if `cd` seems necessary).
- **Shortest unambiguous path** in shell commands (`ls notes/`, not the absolute form).
  Out-of-workspace paths stay absolute, and Read/Edit/Write tool args stay absolute (a
  tool-boundary constraint, not style).
- **One command per shell invocation.** Don't bundle steps (`a && b; c`). Bundling hides which
  step produced which output. Exceptions: a genuine pipeline (`grep | sort`) or a tight,
  inseparable pair where the join is the point.
- **Never mask a command's exit status.** What reads the result sees the invocation's status, so
  a command that fails has to make its invocation fail.
  - never pipe a validating command into `tail` / `grep`, and never `&&` after a piped stage: a
    pipeline's status is the last command's. `${PIPESTATUS[0]}` is the escape hatch when a pipe
    is genuinely wanted
  - never trail one with `; echo "exit=$?"`: that prints the status while the invocation itself
    still exits 0, so the failure is visible only to whoever reads the text
  - to report and still fail: `cmd || { rc=$?; echo failed=$rc; exit $rc; }`. Leave `failed=$rc`
    unquoted: it has no spaces to protect, and the quotes can stop a harness permission rule
    from matching a command it would otherwise allow (wink, 2026-08-05)
- **Scratch files go in repo-local `tmp/`** (gitignored, `mkdir -p tmp` on demand, never
  committed). Prefer it over `/tmp` and the harness scratchpad. `/tmp` is for out-of-project
  temporaries.
- **Read the slice you need** from long notes files. The routine acquaint read is `TODO.md`
  `offset=0, limit=60`. [Notes files](agent-data/notes.md).
- **Use https remotes, not ssh.** Unconditional rather than "when the agent is sandboxed", because
  the remote is chosen at clone time and whether a sandboxed agent will ever touch the repo is not
  knowable then. A sandbox denies ssh twice over: reads of `~/.ssh` are blocked except the signing
  key and `known_hosts`, so no auth key is available, and we think a host allowlist cannot admit
  port 22 at all, since ssh carries no SNI or Host header to match on. The network leg is a
  spawned `git` child that inherits the sandbox, which is why the same config succeeds from a
  human's terminal and fails from a session. So an **ssh remote is the first thing to check when a
  push dies at the network leg**, ahead of any theory about size or timeouts. Both wrong theories
  were held, and eliminated by test, before this rule was written.
  - **Changing a remote's URL needs the user's go**, like any outward-facing change: it moves where
    the repo publishes. Trivially reversible, so this is a confirmation and not a prohibition.
- **Delegate mechanical subtasks to lesser models** (Haiku / Sonnet). Reserve the top model for
  design and tricky work. Top-model tokens are the scarce resource.
- **Don't use the per-project memory directory** (`~/.claude/projects/<path>/memory/`). Durable
  context lives in these committed files: easy for everyone to find beats convenient for the
  bot alone.
- **Mark speculation** in durable text with "We think ..." so a reader can tell the measured
  from the inferred. [Speculation marker](agent-data/prose.md#speculation-marker).
- **End technical explanations in conversation with a plain synopsis**, marked clearly (e.g.
  "The plain version:").
  [Plain synopsis](agent-data/prose.md#plain-synopsis-after-technical-explanations).

## File map

Read every session (`AGENTS.md` is the one file the harness auto-loads, and hard rule 0 covers
the rest of the chain):

- `AGENTS.md`: this file.
- [custom.md](custom.md): the project's layer, and any further file it points at.

Read at the moment of action, immediately before acting, not from memory. The `agent-data/`
files are universal and pinned, listed checklists first, rationale after:

- [cycle-checklists.md](agent-data/cycle-checklists.md): commit / push / opening / close-out
  checklists. Read before any commit work or push.
- [cycle-protocol.md](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md): the full cycle protocol. It wins over any
  checklist summary of it.
- [jj.md](agent-data/jj.md): jj usage, revsets, ochid trailers, the re-describe rule, cycle and
  long-lived bookmarks.
- [prose.md](agent-data/prose.md): prose form, punctuation, commit-title identity. Read before
  writing durable text.
- [notes.md](agent-data/notes.md): TODO / chores / done mechanics, references, anchors. Read
  before editing notes files.
- [code.md](agent-data/code.md): doc comments and unwrap discipline. Read before writing code.
- [versioning.md](agent-data/versioning.md): the version scheme and version-of-record.

Project records (`notes/` and the repo root): records only, never universal rules. Anything
normative that outgrows the project belongs in `agent-data/` via
[Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files):

- `TODO.md`, `notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, `notes/chores/`, `notes/done.md`: the
  project's working records. Conventions are in [agent-data/notes.md](agent-data/notes.md).

## Changing the agent-files

The **agent-files** are `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*`. The official copies are the
template repository's payload, and every member repo carries its own copy of the same set.

- **The payload is the read-only copy.** A member never edits it to experiment. The one thing
  that goes straight in is a *correction*: a factual error, a typo, a stale cross-reference. A
  wrong fact has no second opinion to gather, and leaving it in place misleads every member on
  first read.
- **Intent decides the file, and nothing gates the edit.** A member writes a rule change into its
  local copy of the pinned file whenever it means the family to take it, without asking first.
  The review happens at convergence, on the diff. A change the member does *not* mean the family
  to take goes to `custom.md` and must say why it cannot be family-wide.
- **The diff between a member and the payload *is* that member's open proposal set.** It needs no
  maintenance and cannot go stale.
- **An agent-file change is its own commit**, so `git log -- AGENTS.md agent-data/` reads as a
  list of rule changes rather than unrelated feature titles, and the commit's `ochid:` trailer
  links the bot-repo session that reasoned it out. The diff says what differs now. The history
  says when, by whom, and why.
- **A local agent-file may hold an unagreed experiment**, so unlike the payload it does not read
  as family-agreed. Diff against the payload when that distinction matters.
- **At convergence** the family reviews the members' diffs, folds what it accepts into the
  payload, and every member re-syncs. The diff empties, and the history keeps the record.
- **A resolved experiment retires** like a finished Todo, at the beat where it resolves: see
  [Retiring Done entries](agent-data/notes.md#retiring-done-entries). Adopted and rejected retire
  the same way.

## custom.md: the project layer

[custom.md](custom.md) is the project's own layer and, unlike the pinned files, is never pinned:
every project's content differs by construction. It ships from the payload holding nothing but its
own shape, so a project that changes nothing still has a valid one, and a project adds whatever it
needs: the medium and its validation commands, what a version bump promises this artifact's users,
and its conventions.

**`## Project conventions and overrides` is empty at birth and should usually stay that way.** A
rule the project would keep is still a *proposal* until it is rejected, so by default it belongs in
the pinned file where the rule lives (see [Changing the agent-files](#changing-the-agent-files)),
where it shows up as a diff. Writing it here instead hides it from exactly the review that should
decide it. An empty section stays, with `_None._` under it, rather than being deleted.

**An entry that only points at a further file is not an override** and owes no "why not
family-wide" justification, since it supersedes nothing. A project with a wider context to answer
to can hold all of it in that further file and reach it from one line here, which keeps the rest of
this file identical to the payload's. Nothing pinned names the further file or knows what is in it:
a pinned file asking for something "in custom.md" is answered by following the pointer it finds
there.

Precedence: custom.md is loaded last and wins conflicts with this file and the satellites.

# Notes

This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project.
Each file is organized by topic for easy reference.

By default there are the chores-NN.md files in
[chores/](chores). Chores are general notes about tasks;
short term tasks and their status live at the repo root in
[../TODO.md](../TODO.md). The chores-NN files are numbered
in sequence; the highest-numbered file is the active one,
older ones are closed.

Durable design analyses (measurement theory, error models,
decisions that outlive a cycle) live in
[design.md](design.md). Measurement results that outlive a
cycle (e.g. the thread-placement map) live in their own topic
files — [placement-map.md](placement-map.md). Known defects
awaiting a fix live in [bugs.md](bugs.md); durable
machine/session ops facts in [ops.md](ops.md). For users new
to jj see [jj-tips.md](jj-tips.md).

Examples chore file:
```
# Chores-01.md

General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
how and why of a particular chore.

## Create a binary that lists jj info

This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
and using `jj-lib`
```

## Workflow and conventions

Bot-facing workflow and conventions live in
[`../AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):

- [Notes file conventions](../AGENTS.md#notes-file-conventions)
  — Todo format, Reference numbering, Notes references
  (`[[N]]` citation style), Markdown anchor links, Retiring
  Done entries.
- [Chores conventions](../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) —
  section headers / Done entries exact-title rule, content
  rules, `Commits:` line format.
- [Code Conventions](../AGENTS.md#code-conventions) — doc
  comments, `// OK: …` on `unwrap*` calls, ask-on-ambiguity,
  stuck detection.

Per-cycle workflow lives in
[`cycle-protocol.md`](cycle-protocol.md):

- [Cycles](cycle-protocol.md#cycles): three-phase shape (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out),
  sub-cycles.
- [Step naming](cycle-protocol.md#step-naming): a step is its title, with no number and no
  version.
- [Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow) —

# Notes

This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project.
Each file is organized by topic for easy reference.

By default there are the chores-NN.md files in
[chores/](chores). Chores are general notes about tasks;
short term tasks and their status live at the repo root in
[../TODO.md](../TODO.md). The chores-NN files are numbered
in sequence; the highest-numbered file is the active one,
older ones are closed.

Durable design analyses (measurement theory, error models,
decisions that outlive a cycle) live in
[design.md](design.md). Measurement results that outlive a
cycle (e.g. the thread-placement map) live in their own topic
files — [placement-map.md](placement-map.md). Known defects
awaiting a fix live in [bugs.md](bugs.md); durable
machine/session ops facts in [ops.md](ops.md). For users new
to jj see [jj-tips.md](jj-tips.md).

Examples chore file:
```
# Chores-01.md

General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
how and why of a particular chore.

## Create a binary that lists jj info

This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
and using `jj-lib`
```

## Workflow and conventions

Bot-facing workflow and conventions live in
[`../AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):

- [Notes file conventions](../AGENTS.md#notes-file-conventions)
  — Todo format, Reference numbering, Notes references
  (`[[N]]` citation style), Markdown anchor links, Retiring
  Done entries.
- [Chores conventions](../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) —
  section headers / Done entries exact-title rule, content
  rules, `Commits:` line format.
- [Code Conventions](../AGENTS.md#code-conventions) — doc
  comments, `// OK: …` on `unwrap*` calls, ask-on-ambiguity,
  stuck detection.

Per-cycle workflow lives in
[`cycle-protocol.md`](../agent-data/cycle-protocol.md):

- [Cycles](../agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#cycles): three-phase shape (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out),

The sync is complete in the working tree. Summary of what happened:

**Copied from vc-x1 `main` (73319b8c "docs: consolidate line widths"):**
- `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and all seven `agent-data/` files. `CLAUDE.md` was already identical (`@AGENTS.md`).
- Rename adopted: `agent-data/cycle.md` -> `agent-data/cycle-checklists.md`.
- Relocations adopted: `notes/cycle-protocol.md` and `notes/versioning.md` now live in `agent-data/` as family-universal pinned files. The ours-only content they lose is the old-binary recovery material (the 0.22.0 close-out example) that vc-x1's 2026-08-03 notes already listed as a deliberate drop; jj history keeps it.

**Reference fixes in our project-local files** (the pinned set's internal links were already consistent): `TODO.md` (3 links), `custom-family.md` (2 links), `notes/README.md` (moved-file links now `../agent-data/...`), and the navigational header pointer in `chores-04/05/06.md`. Records' prose mentions of old paths were left as records. Note `notes/README.md` is stale in other ways (links to long-gone `AGENTS.md#chores-conventions` anchors, old `Commits:` line format) — not touched, out of scope.

**Verified:**
- `diff -r` of the copied set against vc-x1 `main` is empty — we are byte-identical to the sync source.
- The two regressions the 2026-08-08 mail flagged are fixed in the adopted text: the per-commit flow's worked example commits via `vc-x1 push` (the one permitted `jj describe` is scratch-title authoring, never published), and the version-bump step is back as step 4 in both checklist and protocol.
- The template payload still differs from this set in every file (~1700 lines total) — expected, since the payload takes the merged set at convergence; our diff against the payload now equals vc-x1's, i.e. the agreed proposal set.

And noted: **`vc-x1-dev` is the binary from here on**, per your instruction (matching the remedy in the 2026-08-06 mail).

The working copy sits uncommitted on top of the `agent-files-model` bookmark. Right — the on-disk files in `../vc-x1` are not their `main`. Their working copy is checked out on the unlanded topic bookmark `docs-freshen-vc-config-and-config-subcmd`, 8 commits ahead of `main`, and as the summary above shows, those draft commits touch `AGENTS.md` and five of the `agent-data/` files (plus a lot of vc-config work).

I synced from their **`main`** (73319b8c "docs: consolidate line widths") deliberately:

- The 2026-08-08 mailbox message names their `main` as the sync source: "your review of our `main`'s agent-files lands".
- By the family's own rules a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands — it can still be rewritten and force-pushed. Syncing from it would adopt text that hasn't passed their own review gate.

You can verify the sync against the right baseline like this — this diff is empty:

```
jj -R ../vc-x1 file show -r main root:AGENTS.md | diff - AGENTS.md
```

and the extraction of their whole `main` set that I diffed against is still in `tmp/vcx1-main-agentfiles/` if you want to check it yourself: `diff -r tmp/vcx1-main-agentfiles/agent-data agent-data` reports nothing.

The plain version: `../vc-x1`'s folder currently shows their work-in-progress branch, not their published `main`. I copied from `main`, so a folder-to-folder diff shows their in-flight edits, not a problem with the sync. When their current cycle lands, a fresh sync would pick up whatever it changed in the agent-files.

134:## Preparation
135-
136-The cycle's first commit, when the cycle needs setup (a
137-lightweight cycle omits it, per
138-[versioning.md](versioning.md#suffix-scheme)):
139-
140-- **Create the cycle's topic bookmark** (commands in
141-  [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
142-- **Bump the version-of-record.** Where it lives, the suffix
143-  scheme, and any derived files (a lockfile, a sourced
144-  manifest version) are project-specific. See
145-  [versioning.md](versioning.md).
146-- **Move a `## Todo` item** (if the cycle has one) into
147-  `## In Progress`, and write the cycle's **six provisional
148-  items** there. All six are required, all six are revised
149-  as steps land, and all six move to chores at close-out.
150-  The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress`'s
151-  own, and the other five are headings one level below the
152-  title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items; under a
153-  program heading, each one deeper):
154-  - the **title**, which becomes the chores section header.
155-  - the **problem statement**: what is wrong, in a sentence
156-    or two.
157-  - the **solution statement**: what will be done about it,
158-    broad. Provisional here, since it is written before the
159-    work. The close-out's commit body carries the final one.
160-  - the **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you
161-    finished?". Not the per-commit validation, which asks
162-    whether the artifact still works. This asks whether the
163-    thing the cycle promised actually happened, specifically
164-    enough that a reader can run it.
165-  - the **ladder**: one rung per step, in the form
166-    `- [[N]] [<title>][M] (marker)` described below.
167-  - the **deliberation**: how the five above were decided,
168-    alternatives weighed, costs accepted. `_None._` when
169-    there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real answer
170-    and different from having forgotten to write it.
171-
172-The ladder is a linked table of contents. A rung is `- [[N]] [<title>][M] (marker)` and
173-carries no detail beyond that:
174-
175-- The literal `[[N]]` is the as-built ladder's placeholder, carried from birth. It fills only
176-  at backfill after landing (see [Commits backfill](#commits-backfill)), so the close-out move
177-  just drops the `(current)` / `(done)` markers.
178-- The title links to the rung's subsection below, reference-style: `[M]` is a file-local slot
179-  whose definition is a same-file fragment, `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References` (slug
180-  algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). Routing through the
181-  table keeps rung lines short, and the close-out move renumbers the slots like any other rung
182-  ref.
183-
184-The verbiage lives in the rung's subsection under a **`Ladder details`** heading following the
185-deliberation, headed by the rung's exact title, so it is greppable and an anchor other records
186-can link. Every rung but the close-out has one, written in two beats:
187-
188-- **Opened at laddering** with an abstract-sized intent statement: the rung's problem and
189-  solution in a sentence or two, provisional like the rest of the block, so a rung nobody has
190-  started is described by more than its title.
191-- **Completed at the rung's landing** with the conceptual delta (design points, consequences,
192-  deferrals). It never restates the landed commit body's problem/solution: the body is the
193-  record, and the subsection keeps only what the body does not say.

# Todo

This file contains near term tasks with a short description
and reference links to more details.

Intro paragraphs in `## Todo` and `## Bugs` should begin every
line with 1 leading space so they don't match the `^\d+\. `
pattern that locates numbered entries; 2 or 3 spaces also work.

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. At Preparation
the picked-up `## Todo` item **moves** here (never copied, one home per text) and becomes six
provisional items, all required, all revised as steps land. At close-out the whole block moves
into `notes/chores/chores-NN.md` and becomes that cycle's `##` section. It is never written in
two places. Shape:

```
### <type>: <title>

#### Problem
<what is wrong, a sentence or two>

#### Solution
<what will be done about it, broad; provisional until the close-out>

#### Acceptance check
<the measure of "are you finished?">

#### Ladder
- [[N]] [<cycle title> opening][M] (done)
- [[N]] [<title>][M] (current)
- [[N]] [<title>][M]
- [[N]] <cycle title> closing

#### Deliberation
<how the five above were decided; `_None._` if there was nothing to deliberate>

#### Ladder details
<one `#####` subsection per rung, headed by its exact title, opened at laddering with the
rung's intent and completed at landing with the conceptual delta; the closing rung's only at
close-out, gotchas in problem/solution form>
```

A multi-cycle program adds one level: the program is the `###`, its current cycle the `####`,
and the six items sit one level below that (headings give the current work durable anchors,
which numbered Todo entries can't). Full rules in
[cycle-protocol.md](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#preparation); the move's four transforms are
in [Chores sections](agent-data/cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

The re-sync is done. The pinned set is now byte-identical to vc-x1's `docs-freshen-vc-config-and-config-subcmd` bookmark tip (3ae26bad) — the agent-files that match the `vc-x1-dev` binary we're now using.

What the bookmark's version adds over their `main`, in substance:

- **Hard rules gain an exceptions clause**: rules bind the bot, none is absolute — wink can bend any rule explicitly in the moment or by scoped delegation, and every taken exception is recorded; nothing bends silently.
- **Rule 13 tightened**: the bookmark is named by the cycle title's slug, carries every step, and is deleted locally and remotely once landed. The bot repo needs no bookmark.
- **New "Cycle" terminology entry**: single-step folds all three stages into one commit; multi-step is minimum two commits.
- **Convention work runs as its own cycle**, never as an inserted rung mid-feature.
- **The ladder is now a linked table of contents**: rungs are `- [[N]] [<title>][M] (marker)` with reference-style links to per-rung `Ladder details` subsections, opened at laddering with intent and completed at landing with the conceptual delta.

Follow-up edits that came with it: our `TODO.md`'s `## In Progress` preamble now carries the new six-item shape (mirrored from their TODO.md, including the multi-cycle program note).
